text:
sam_infra: Kicking off aurora-edge region bring-up. Primary goals: wire TF provisioning modules to Pulumi statebridge, sanity-check networking (VPC/subnets/peerings), and get CI/state locking solid before handoff. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/aurora-edge/pulls/34 :eyes:

maya_devex: Thanks — can you drop the golden-path checklist here? I’ll convert to runbook after we validate.

sam_infra: Quick checklist (happy to expand):
- validate TF modules import to statebridge
- ensure remote state backend locked and migration plan reviewed
- run pulumi preview against env (staging -> aurora-edge)
- confirm quota for desired GPU SKU (A100/80GB) with cloud team
- BGP/peering config + egress IP ranges checked
- cost estimate + burst policy for Dedicated
- minimal canary: 1 nodepool with 2 GPUs, 3 nodes, autoscale off for initial validation

lee_platform: On the TF->Pulumi binding: watch out for resource address drift when moving state. Use the state-mapping script in infra-scripts: `scripts/statebridge/migrate-mapping.py` and run in dry-run mode first.

noah_oncall: FYI, last time we had the routing issue it was because subnets overlapped with partner VPC (corp-data). Double-check `10.200.0.0/16` is unused.

zoe_sre: Also add health checks for the serving runtime: kernel version, cuda drivers, and NVLINK visibility. I have a small probe we can run via DaemonSet: `kubectl apply -f tools/gpu-probe.yaml` — it reports missing drivers to #incidents if failures > 10%.

sam_infra: Ran `pulumi preview` against staging-aurora-edge. Output snippet:```
Previewing update (dev)
  pulumi:pulumi:Stack aurora-edge-dev updating
  3 to create, 0 to update, 0 to delete
  + redwood:network:VPC aurora-vpc
  + redwood:compute:NodePool gpu-np-1
```
No drift detected on resources we imported, but bucket ACLs will change — flagged in PR.

maya_devex: Great. Can you paste the exact `terraform state` commands you used for the import? I’ll add them to runbook.

sam_infra: Sure: `terraform import -state=/tmp/aurora.tfstate module.vpc.google_compute_network.vpc projects/redwood-prod/global/networks/aurora-vpc` then `terraform state rm module.vpc.google_compute_subnetwork.subnet` (we stashed subnet management in Pulumi). Ran the mapping script after.

prashant_net: GPU quota: cloud quota says only 24 A100s available in aurora region right now. If we need more we need ticket to infra-ops for capacity request, ETA ~72h. Suggest using mixed SKU for initial canary (1xA100 + 2xA10) to stay under quota.

noah_oncall: Also, for CI wiring: make sure the pipeline uses a temporary state lock key `locks/aurora-edge-<run-id>` and that the cleanup step always runs, even on failure. We had a stuck lock for 3h last time.

sam_infra: Noted. I added a `post` job in .gitlab-ci.yml to delete the lock key and a watcher job that alerts #eng-oncall if lock > 15m.

zoe_sre: Preflight validation steps I ran locally:
1) `gcloud compute networks list --filter=aurora` (confirm no collisions)
2) `pulumi preview --diff` (check ACLs)
3) `kubectl apply -f tools/gpu-probe.yaml` (validate drivers)
4) `./tools/cost-estimator --region aurora-edge --nodepool gpu-np-1` (artifact attached)
All green except cost shows ~12% higher egress due to cross-region peering.

maya_devex: I’ll draft the runbook sections: bootstrap, validation, and handoff. Handoff will require: team oncall, runbook link, list of tags/labels, and a rollback plan.

lee_platform: For rollback, keep the previous TF state snapshot in `backups/aurora-edge/` and have a `terraform apply -state=backups/aurora-edge/previous.tfstate` plan ready. Also tag images with `aurora-edge-canary-<sha>` to revert quickly.

sam_infra: Opening a follow-up task: infra#487 — finish runbook, add pipeline lock cleanup, request quota expansion if green after smoke. Assigning to @maya_devex, @prashant_net for quota comms.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline started for branch `feature/aurora-edge-sync` — job 1225. Logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/1225

prashant_net: I'll file the quota ticket now and ping cloud-quotas. ETA 72h but will push for expedited if we can commit to reserved capacity.

noah_oncall: After initial canary, schedule a 1-hour burn-in (load test) between 02:00-03:00 UTC to validate autoscaling thresholds. I’ll be on-call for that window.

sam_infra: Perfect. Next steps: Maya to write runbook draft + validation checklist, Prashant to manage quota ticket, Lee to validate state-mapping script output, Zoe to attach probe results to runbook, Noah to coordinate burn-in. Will handoff to eng-sre once burn-in passes. :thumbsup:

maya_devex: Copying plan into runbook draft now https://docs.redwood/runbooks/aurora-edge (will update with exact commands).

sam_infra: Thanks everyone. If you hit any blockers call me or ping #pager.

zoe_sre: small note — add cost tag `redwood:project=aurora-edge` to all resources. Helps chargeback reports.

sam_infra: done, added tag to TF vars.

infra-bot: Job 1225 succeeded. Artifacts: `pulumi-preview.txt`, `state-mapping-dryrun.log`.

maya_devex: will continue in runbook PR and ping for review after I finish the bootstrap/validation sections.

lee_platform: I ran the mapping dry-run — looks clean except one bucket name collision; renaming in PR.

sam_infra: closing thread for now — will reopen if any of the validation steps fail. Thanks all.
